title: Functions
short_description: Write reusable blocks of code and pass inputs.
bro_quote: Functions transform repetitive code into reusable tools—write once, use everywhere.

subtopics.name: Creating Functions
subtopics.explanation:
• 📦 Use def to create a function.
  • 📞 Call it by its name with parentheses.
  • 💡 Functions group code for reusability and clarity.

snippets.code:
def say_goodbye():
    print("See you later!")
    print("Goodbye!")

say_goodbye()

def celebrate():
    print("🎉 Party time!")

celebrate()
celebrate()
celebrate()

subtopics.name: Parameters and Returns
subtopics.explanation:
• 🎛️ Parameters are inputs that functions receive.
  • 🎁 return sends results back to the caller.
  • ✅ Return stops the function immediately.
  • 📊 Functions can return any data type: numbers, strings, lists, etc.

snippets.code:
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

result = add(5, 3)
print(result)

def greet_person(name):
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

msg = greet_person("Alice")
print(msg)

subtopics.name: Default Parameters
subtopics.explanation:
• 🎯 Set default values for parameters.
  • ⚡ Call function without that parameter to use the default.
  • 💼 Makes functions flexible and easier to use.

snippets.code:
def greet(name="Guest"):
    print(f"Welcome, {name}!")

greet()           # Uses default
greet("Bob")     # Overrides default

def power(base, exponent=2):
    return base ** exponent

print(power(5))      # 25 (5^2)
print(power(5, 3))   # 125 (5^3)

subtopics.name: Multiple Return Values
subtopics.explanation:
• 📦 Return multiple values as a tuple.
  • 🔀 Unpack them into separate variables.
  • 🎪 Useful for functions that compute several things.

snippets.code:
def divide(a, b):
    quotient = a // b
    remainder = a % b
    return quotient, remainder

q, r = divide(17, 5)
print(f"Quotient: {q}, Remainder: {r}")

def analyze_list(nums):
    total = sum(nums)
    count = len(nums)
    return total, count

total, size = analyze_list([10, 20, 30])
print(f"Sum: {total}, Count: {size}")

subtopics.name: Scope: Local vs Global
subtopics.explanation:
• 🔒 Local variables only exist inside functions.
  • 🌍 Global variables exist throughout the program.
  • ⚠️ Use global keyword to modify global variables in functions.
  • 🎯 Local scope is usually safer and cleaner.

snippets.code:
def calculate():
    x = 100
    print(x)

calculate()  # Prints 100
# print(x)   # Error! x doesn't exist outside

counter = 0

def increment():
    global counter
    counter += 1

increment()
increment()
print(counter)  # 2

subtopics.name: Docstrings
subtopics.explanation:
• 📝 Document what your function does with docstrings.
  • 📖 Use triple quotes """..."""` at the start of the function.
  • 🔍 Helps others (and future you) understand the code.

snippets.code:
def calculate_area(length, width):
    """Calculate the area of a rectangle.
    Args: length and width
    Returns: area as a number"""
    return length * width

print(calculate_area(5, 10))

subtopics.name: Lambda Functions (Quick Functions)
subtopics.explanation:
• ⚡ One-line functions using lambda keyword.
  • 🎯 Perfect for short, simple operations.
  • 🔧 Often used with map(), filter(), sorted().

snippets.code:
square = lambda x: x ** 2
print(square(5))  # 25

add = lambda x, y: x + y
print(add(3, 7))  # 10

numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4]
squares = list(map(lambda x: x ** 2, numbers))
print(squares)  # [1, 4, 9, 16]

questions: 1. Define a function called say_hello that prints a greeting. (Defining function)
2. Call a function you just defined to execute its code. (Calling function)
3. Write a function that takes one parameter (a name) and greets that person. (Single parameter)
4. Create a function that accepts two numbers and calculates their product. (Multiple parameters)
5. Write a function that returns the square of a number instead of printing it. (Return value)
6. Make a function return both the sum and difference of two numbers. (Returning multiple values)
7. Add a default value of 'Guest' to a name parameter in a greeting function. (Default parameter)
8. Call a function explicitly mentioning the parameter names. (Keyword args)
9. Create a variable inside a function and try to print it outside to see what happens. (Local scope)
10. Call a previously created math function twice with different sets of numbers. (Reusability)
